checks_run.procedure: Adversarial hunt for any path that stores, audits or returns something unfaithful or undeclared for strings that are not well-formed: OIDC claims other than iss/sub (name, preferred_username, email, astral sub at the 255/256 code-point boundary); callback query values and keys with CESU-8/invalid percent bytes; raw ill-formed UTF-8 bytes in JSON bodies (Content-Length and chunked, authenticated and unauthenticated); header bytes over a real socket (User-Agent stored in session, X-Request-Id); and a U+FFFD sweep of user_identity, app_user, session and audit_event
checks_run.command: with-pg.sh 55771|55772 pnpm vitest run --project integration zz-sec-r7-probe.test.ts --reporter=verbose; node probes/fastify-invalid-utf8-errcode.mjs (cwd <clone>/apps/api)
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone $TMPDIR/probe at 90439483; Node 22.22.2; Fastify 5.6.1 (locked); disposable PostgreSQL 16 (LANG unset and C.UTF-8); real TCP socket on 127.0.0.1:0
checks_run.expected: Every residual is either shown absent, or recorded as a finding with a reproduction, severity and owner
checks_run.actual: Absent (both runs): A1-A5, C1-C2 and E1 pass. A sub of 255 astral code points is stored verbatim, and 256 is an audited token_invalid. Claims carrying lone surrogates fall back without U+FFFD and never bind a look-alike e-mail. The callback always answers a declared 302. Headers are Latin-1 decoded, so they cannot hold a surrogate: the User-Agent is stored as its exact, well-formed Latin-1 reading. X-Request-Id is never reflected. The audit, identity, user and session tables hold no U+FFFD. One residual was found, so vitest exits 1 (B1, B2): raw invalid UTF-8 bytes in a JSON body give an undeclared 500 internal when sent with a Content-Length, even unauthenticated (500 before 401). The cause is FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_CONTENT_LENGTH, unmapped in hooks.ts mapError. B3: sent chunked, the bytes are stored and audited as U+FFFD. Raised as F-DG2-290 (Low, non-mandatory) with a reproduction and an owner.

checks_run.procedure: Review the product diff 51a692b1..90439483 (27 files). BE11 sweep (assignments, sessions, gates, criteria, relay, evidence X-File-Name, OIDC routes): no behaviour change beyond code-point-safe truncation. BE12 (framework-errors.ts, server.ts, hooks.ts problemForError): HELMET_OPTIONS equals the previous inline CSP; error responses carry the same security headers; no internals or raw URL leak; frameworkErrors and clientErrorHandler cannot bypass authz or rate limiting. Judge D-067's 408. Scan the added lines for secrets, CDN, eval and SQL grants.
checks_run.command: git diff 51a692b1..90439483 -- . ':!docs/delivery'; grep scan of '^+' lines; diff of the CSP block at 51a692b1 vs HELMET_OPTIONS at 90439483; git diff -- docs/api/openapi.yaml package.json pnpm-lock.yaml .github deploy packages/db/migrations | wc -l; zz-sec-r7-probe part D over a real socket
checks_run.environment: Working tree (git) and disposable clone $TMPDIR/probe at 90439483; Node 22.22.2; disposable PostgreSQL 16
checks_run.expected: No regression to authorization, sessions or integrity; CSP identical; error responses problem-shaped with the routed security headers and no echo; no secrets or CDN
checks_run.actual: Scan hits: test fixtures only ('https://idp.example.invalid', 'http://localhost:3000', 'http://synthetic.invalid'). The contract, lockfile, CI, deploy and migrations are unchanged (0 diff lines). The CSP directives are identical. captureSecurityHeaders copies helmet's own output from a throwaway instance, so the values cannot drift. Over a real socket, D1 gives 400 problem+json with validation.format / headers_too_large / malformed_request for: a CESU path, %ZZ on an unauthenticated POST, header and URL overflow, NUL in a header, and a garbage line. Every one carries the 12 security headers identical to a routed 404's. requestId equals X-Request-Id. Nothing is echoed (no FST_ERR/HPE_/%ED/%ZZ/payload). '%0d%0a' in the path injects no header. D2: a bad URL on a protected mutation writes nothing and leaves no audit row. No handler, hook or database access runs, so there is no authorization bypass. Rate limiting is global at onRequest, so it is unaffected. D3 (pipelined garbage) behaves like Fastify's default handler; BE12 is stricter because it never writes into a started response. The BE11 truncations only swap .slice for truncateText. The callback try/catch maps only SQLSTATE class 22 and 23514 and rethrows the rest. D-067's 408: Node's requestTimeout answers before any operation is matched; Fastify's default also sent 408, now as a problem body. I judge documenting it as transport-level acceptable, consistent with the shared 404 and 500 treatment.

summary: PASS. F-DG2-260 is CLOSED_VERIFIED. My round-6 repro passes unchanged: JIT and bind get the declared 302 token_invalid with a session.login_failed row and nothing created, and a jsonb text gets 400 validation.invalid_character at its pointer. The adversarial hunt finds no lone-surrogate residual in claims, the callback query, headers, the path or audit_event. BE11 changes only the truncation. BE12 keeps the CSP identical, gives every pre-routing error a problem+json body with the routed security headers and no echo, and opens no authorization or rate-limit bypass. D-067's 408 is acceptable. One new Low, non-mandatory finding: F-DG2-290, where raw invalid UTF-8 bytes in a JSON body give an undeclared 500 (even unauthenticated) or, when chunked, are stored as U+FFFD. All required checks ran and passed: build, typecheck, lint, openapi:lint (161), no-cdn and format; unit tests 673/673 on Node 22, Node 24 and under load; integration 531/531 twice (LANG unset and C.UTF-8); AUD-403 146/146; historical validation of DG0 and DG1.
